html:
The Akaitcho territory is the land of the Dene east of Great Slave Lake, in the Northwest Territories of Canada, home to the Yellowknives Dene and their neighbours. It is named for Akaitcho (about 1786 to 1838), a Yellowknives chief. The Yellowknives speak a form of the Dënësųłinë́ language, part of the Athabaskan family.

They hunted caribou on the edge of the tundra and traded furs, and took their name from the copper knives they made. Akaitcho guided and fed the British naval officer John Franklin on his first Arctic overland expedition of 1819 to 1822, without which the party would not have survived.

The Dene of the area signed Treaty 8 in 1900. Today the Akaitcho Dene First Nations are negotiating a land claim with Canada. Neighbours: NWT Métis and Dene Tha'.
